title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 149 (Delivery to bailee how made)

content.overview: Section 149 provides that the delivery to the bailee may be made by doing anything which has the effect of putting the goods in the possession of the intended bailee or of any person authorised to hold them on his behalf.
content.glance: Delivery to the bailee is effected by any act that puts the goods in the possession of the intended bailee or of a person authorised to hold them for him.
content.study: The delivery to the bailee may be made by doing anything which has the effect of putting the goods in the possession of the intended bailee or of any person authorised to hold them on his behalf. Current-law framing: delivery may be actual or constructive; the essential is transfer of possession/control.

sections.heading: Core rule
sections.body: The delivery to the bailee may be made by doing anything which has the effect of putting the goods in the possession of the intended bailee or of any person authorised to hold them on his behalf.

examples.title: Delivery by key or authorisation
examples.body: Handing over the key of a warehouse or authorising a third person to take possession effects delivery under Section 149.

hypotheticals.question: A tells B to take the goods from A’s premises and B does so. Is delivery complete?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes. Section 149 provides that delivery may be made by anything that puts the goods in the possession of the intended bailee.

learningObjectives: State how delivery to a bailee is effected under Section 149.
enhancement.definition: The delivery to the bailee may be made by doing anything which has the effect of putting the goods in the possession of the intended bailee or of any person authorised to hold them on his behalf.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Delivery is completed by any act that transfers possession to the bailee or an authorised holder.
essentialIngredients: Act that puts the goods in the possession of the intended bailee or authorised person
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 149 provides that delivery to the bailee may be made by doing anything which has the effect of putting the goods in the possession of the intended bailee or of any person authorised to hold them on his behalf. Delivery may therefore be actual or constructive.
examples: Handing keys or authorising collection constitutes delivery.
distinctions: Section 149 concerns the mode of delivery; Section 148 defines bailment itself.
problemApplication: Identify the act that transferred possession.
Conclude whether delivery under Section 149 is complete.
keyTakeaways: Delivery is effected by any act putting the goods in the bailee’s (or authorised person’s) possession.

distinctions.title: Scope of s-149
distinctions.body: Applies only within the elements and consequences stated in the statutory text.

misconceptions.myth: s-149 creates unlimited or extra-statutory rights.
misconceptions.correction: It operates only as stated in the provision.
